one_liner: C++17 JPEG-LS (ISO 14495-1) lossless/near-lossless codec; encodes about 10x faster than libwebp lossless, decodes slower.
what_it_does: CharLS implements the baseline JPEG-LS standard (LOCO-I) for 2- to 16-bit grayscale and 2-4 component images, lossless or near-lossless, and is the JPEG-LS codec behind GDCM and other DICOM stacks. It exposes a C ABI (charls_jpegls_encoder_* / charls_jpegls_decoder_* handles returning charls_jpegls_errc) plus C++ wrapper classes charls::jpegls_encoder and charls::jpegls_decoder that work on caller-supplied memory buffers with optional stride. It is a different format from PNG or WebP, not a drop-in for libpng or libwebp; you choose it when you need JPEG-LS files (DICOM transfer syntaxes, .jls) or a cheap symmetric lossless codec.
how_it_is_fast: The algorithm itself is light: per-pixel median edge detector (MED) prediction, gradient-quantized context modeling with bias correction, adaptive Golomb-Rice coding of residuals and a run mode for flat regions. CharLS compiles specialized codecs per sample type through C++ templates and traits (lossless_traits for 8/16-bit pair/triplet/quad pixels in sample-interleaved mode), uses precomputed gradient-quantization LUTs and per-k Golomb decode LUTs for codes of 8 bits or less, a 64-bit bit cache read with big-endian unaligned loads plus memchr to skip ahead to the next 0xFF stuffing byte, and countl_zero for unary prefixes. There is no SIMD; unreleased main-branch PRs by cl445 add more (#361 skips sample reconstruction in the lossless encoder: 473 to 452 ms on Ryzen 9 9950X/GCC 14, 428 to 370 ms on Apple Silicon for a 7680x4320 12-bit image; #376 PGO-derived branch hints and cold-path outlining: decode 8.5% and encode 3.6% faster on x86-64 Clang 20 for one 7216x5412 8-bit image), none of which the catalogued 2.4.2 numbers include.
when_to_use: You must read or write JPEG-LS: DICOM transfer syntaxes 1.2.840.10008.1.2.4.80/.81, remote sensing or archives that mandate an ISO standard lossless codec.

Lossless encoding of 8-bit RGB or grayscale at high volume where encode time matters more than file size: about 10x faster encode than libwebp lossless (quality=100) and 4.6x faster than Pillow's zlib PNG on CLIC2021.
12- to 16-bit medical, scientific or camera-raw-like single-channel images, which PNG handles poorly and QOI-family codecs do not support.
Near-lossless coding with a hard per-pixel error bound (NEAR parameter), which the PNG/QOI siblings cannot do.
You want a mature, standards-conformant library with a stable C ABI, vcpkg/Conan packages and .NET, WebAssembly and Python adapters.
when_not_to_use: Decode-heavy workloads of 8-bit RGB: in the CLIC2021 run CharLS decoded about 1.8x slower than libwebp lossless m1 and about 2x slower than Pillow's zlib PNG decoder.
When ratio is the goal: its CLIC2021 output was 29% larger than WebP lossless m1 and larger than JPEG XL -e1, which also encoded faster (43.0 s vs 72.2 s).
When raw speed with any format is acceptable: QOI, QOIR, fNBLI and HALIC beat it on both encode and decode in the same table.
Web delivery: browsers do not decode JPEG-LS.

Files using JPEG-LS Part 2 extensions, encoded restart markers, subsampled scans or point transform: the README lists these as unsupported (restart markers decode only, with no recovery for corrupted streams).

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (CMake, vcpkg, Conan; source-only, no binary releases)
integration.min_toolchain: main branch: C++17, CMake 3.22, GCC 9.1, Clang 7, MSVC 2019, Apple Clang 12; 2.x LTS branch: C++14
integration.platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS on x86, x64, arm, arm64, mips, s390x, ppc64le (big-endian fixed in 2.3.3); portable C++, no SIMD
integration.thread_safety: not documented; each encoder/decoder is a separate handle and the shared Golomb and quantization tables are immutable statics (read from source), so one instance per thread is the safe pattern

gotchas: Releases 2.3.0 through 2.4.3 have GHSA-mqrg-gfc8-73ff (CVSS 5.3): a crafted oversize-dimension LSE marker wraps pixel_stride and causes out-of-bounds access; fixed in 2.4.4, which caps width and height at 100000. pillow-jpls 1.3.2, still the latest wheel on PyPI and the one benchmarked, statically links vulnerable CharLS 2.4.2.

main is the unreleased 3.0 with breaking API changes (charls.h split into charls.h/charls.hpp, legacy 1.x API removed, include_pc_parameters_jai no longer default); 2.4.4 is the latest tagged release.
Hewlett Packard claims JPEG-LS patents, licensed free for conformant implementations; the README tells commercial users to check hpl.hp.com/loco.
The fast specialized paths cover lossless 8-bit and 16-bit data (sample-interleaved pairs, triplets and quads); near-lossless and other bit depths go through the generic default_traits path.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick CharLS over QOI, QOIR, fNBLI or HALIC when you need an ISO/ITU standard format (DICOM) or more than 8 bits per sample; pick fpng/fpnge or libjxl fast_lossless instead when you need browser-readable output, and OpenJPH when the format is HTJ2K rather than JPEG-LS.
verified_claims_summary: In WangXuan95/Image-Compression-Benchmark (CLIC2021, 585 RGB images, 4.1 GB, single thread, Intel i7-12700H, Windows 10), CharLS 2.4.2 via the pillow-jpls 1.3.2 wheel took 72.2 s to encode and 66.6 s to decode versus 720.2 s / 37.0 s for libwebp lossless m1 and 334.8 s / 33.7 s for Pillow's zlib PNG, so it wins on encode only. The times include Python Image.open/save and PNM file I/O per image, the wheel's compiler flags are unstated, and RunBenchmark.py ships with CHECK_DISTORTION = False, so lossless round-trips are not checked by default.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-02; 2.4.4 security release in June 2026, 3.0 encoder speedups merged on main), BSD-3-Clause and copyable, with libFuzzer/AFL harness options in the build.
